project_title: Brain insulin resistance across dementias: shared mechanism, disease-specific phenotype, or downstream consequence?
research_question: Is the phenomenon commonly described as type 3 diabetes or brain insulin resistance the same biological process across major dementias, and at what point in each disease trajectory does it first become demonstrable?

scientific_models.name: shared_early_mechanism
scientific_models.summary: A common early brain-insulin-resistance process contributes causally across multiple dementias.
predictions: comparable insulin-signaling defects across dementia pathologies
abnormalities detectable before substantial neuronal loss
effects persist after accounting for systemic diabetes
shared signaling nodes across diseases
insulin-directed interventions affect downstream disease biology across multiple dementias

scientific_models.name: alzheimer_specific_phenotype
scientific_models.summary: The classical type-3-diabetes phenotype is predominantly Alzheimer-related.
predictions: intrinsic neuronal insulin resistance is stronger or qualitatively different in AD
non-AD dementias show weaker or different brain insulin phenotypes
abnormalities track amyloid/tau biology more closely than other proteinopathies
head-to-head comparisons discriminate AD from non-AD disease

scientific_models.name: disease_specific_metabolic_phenotypes
scientific_models.summary: Different dementias disrupt insulin-related pathways through different mechanisms and compartments.
predictions: AD, Lewy-body disease, FTD and vascular disease have distinct pathway signatures
cellular compartment differs by disease
genotype/pathology-specific signatures occur within FTD and familial dementias
no single cross-dementia molecular definition captures all cases

scientific_models.name: secondary_convergence
scientific_models.summary: Insulin-signaling dysfunction is mainly a downstream convergence of established neurodegeneration, inflammation, proteinopathy, or energetic failure.
predictions: abnormality increases with disease burden
early stages show weak or inconsistent insulin defects
different initiating pathologies converge on similar late metabolic failure
insulin correction may improve function without altering initiating pathology

scientific_models.name: systemic_or_confounding
scientific_models.summary: Much of the association is explained by peripheral insulin resistance, vascular disease, age, obesity, medications, frailty, or ascertainment.
predictions: effects attenuate with rigorous metabolic and vascular adjustment
peripheral proxies show stronger effects than direct brain measures
vascular and mixed dementias show the strongest associations
intrinsic brain insulin resistance independent of systemic disease is uncommon

dementia_strata: primary progressive aphasia when mechanistically relevant
comparators: other neurodegenerative disease controls when available

evidence_directness_hierarchy.label: functional_human_brain_insulin_response
examples: ex vivo insulin stimulation of human brain tissue
receptor/pathway response before versus after insulin exposure

evidence_directness_hierarchy.label: mechanistically_linked_neuroimaging
examples: imaging response to insulin challenge or validated insulin-linked imaging paradigm

non_equivalence_rules: Peripheral insulin resistance does not by itself demonstrate brain insulin resistance.
FDG-PET hypometabolism does not by itself demonstrate insulin resistance.
Altered abundance of an insulin-pathway protein does not by itself demonstrate functional insulin resistance.
Cross-sectional severity association does not establish temporal precedence or onset.
LLM agreement does not constitute scientific replication.

temporal_analysis.primary_goal: Reconstruct the earliest defensible detection of insulin-signaling abnormality in each dementia and its ordering relative to defining pathology and neurodegeneration.

temporal_claim_classes.T1_direct_precedence: Longitudinal evidence demonstrates insulin abnormality before a defined pathology, clinical transition, or neurodegenerative endpoint.
temporal_claim_classes.T2_anchored_early_presence: Abnormality is directly observed at a preclinical/prodromal stage, but precedence over pathology is not demonstrated.
temporal_claim_classes.T3_stage_association_only: Cross-sectional or stage-correlated evidence without onset inference.
temporal_claim_classes.T4_retrospective_or_proxy: Timing is inferred from retrospective reports, peripheral proxies, unvalidated biomarkers, or indirect measures.

hard_rules: Never convert T2, T3, or T4 evidence into T1 precedence.
For cross-sectional studies, time_relation_to_pathology may be coexisting, earlier_stage_presence, or unresolved, but not demonstrated_precedence.
Earliest observed abnormality is not synonymous with biological onset.
If disease stage or pathology status is ambiguous, set temporal_claim_class to T5_onset_unresolved unless another defensible classification applies.
Use intervals or stage ranges; do not invent a single onset age.
Separate temporal ordering relative to diagnosis from ordering relative to molecular pathology.

measurement_validity_audit.known_priority_example: L1CAM-based neuron-derived extracellular-vesicle claims must be linked to later L1CAM/EV validation literature rather than accepted at face value.

shared_discriminator_questions: Is the abnormality demonstrated directly in brain tissue or only via systemic/proxy measures?
Which cellular compartment and brain region are affected?
Is the molecular direction and pathway node the same across dementias?
Does the abnormality persist after controlling for systemic diabetes, obesity, vascular disease, age, medications and frailty?
Is the finding independently replicated in distinct study families, cohorts, laboratories or analytic pipelines?
What is the earliest defensible disease stage at which the abnormality is observed?
Does evidence demonstrate that insulin-signaling dysfunction precedes defining pathology or only coexist with it?
Would the same result be expected in a patient with comparable neurodegeneration but a different underlying dementia?
Does insulin-directed intervention modify disease biology, symptoms only, or neither?
Could the observed association be explained by measurement artefact, selection, treatment exposure or publication bias?

citation_expansion.saturation: Stop only after two consecutive low-yield cycles, including at least one with zero new eligible study families, plus completion of pivotal citation chasing and unresolved-gap classification.

llm_execution.rule: Model agreement is a quality-control signal only and must never increment scientific replication counts.

decision_rule: Preserve uncertainty. Do not force a winning model when directness, temporality, replication or measurement validity are insufficient.
